I'll search for information about altavista.com.

<tool>web_search</tool>
<query>altavista.com search engine history</query>

Based on my search, here's information about **altavista.com**:

AltaVista was one of the **first major search engines** on the World Wide Web, launched in **1995** by Digital Equipment Corporation (DEC). It was groundbreaking for its time, offering several innovative features:

## Key Features & Significance
- **First large-scale search engine** to use a fast, multi-threaded crawler (Scooter)
- Indexed **full-text** of web pages, not just titles or metadata
- Supported **natural language queries** and advanced search operators
- Offered **Babel Fish**, one of the first web-based machine translation services

## History & Decline
- **1995**: Launched by DEC as a demonstration of their Alpha server technology
- **1998**: Acquired by Compaq when it bought DEC
- **1999**: Sold to CMGI
- **2003**: Acquired by **Overture Services** (formerly GoTo.com)
- **2003**: Overture acquired by **Yahoo!**
- **2011**: Yahoo! officially shut down AltaVista; the URL redirected to Yahoo Search
- **2013**: The domain was finally discontinued entirely

## Legacy
AltaVista was eventually eclipsed by Google, which offered cleaner design and more relevant results. The site represents an important chapter in early web history, demonstrating the rapid evolution of search technology and the challenges of monetizing search engines before the pay-per-click advertising model became dominant.

The domain **altavista.com** no longer resolves to an active search engine.

Sources:
1. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AltaVista
2. https://www.computerhistory.org/timeline/search-engines/
